front: Cairnway wants a foundation model with no servers to manage. Amazon Bedrock or SageMaker AI?
back: Amazon Bedrock. It uses models someone else built and hosts. SageMaker AI is for building, training and hosting your own model with full control.

front: Where does Amazon SageMaker JumpStart fit relative to SageMaker AI?
back: JumpStart is the machine learning hub inside SageMaker AI. It lets you compare pretrained models, customize them with your data and deploy them into your own SageMaker environment.

front: Cairnway's marketing and finance staff want AI help and dashboards without writing code. Which AWS option fits?
back: Amazon Quick, an AI workspace for business users. Kiro is for developers, and Strands Agents and AgentCore are for building and running agents.

front: Strands Agents versus Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: which builds the agent and which runs it?
back: Strands Agents is the open-source toolkit for writing the agent in code. AgentCore is the platform that hosts and operates it in production, with runtime, memory, gateway, identity, policy and observability.

front: What is Kiro for, and who uses it?
back: Kiro is an agentic AI engineering system that helps developers plan, build, review and verify software. It is aimed at the developers themselves, not at business users.

front: Cairnway needs a demand-forecasting model trained on three years of sales history. Which service?
back: Amazon SageMaker AI. This is training a custom model, not a foundation-model task, so full control over training and hosting is needed.

front: What does the principle 'do not build what you can use, and do not host what you can have managed' mean?
back: Choose the highest layer that meets the requirement. Use a ready-made tool first, then a managed service, and build and host your own model only when you truly need that control.

front: How do AWS managed services lower the barrier to entry?
back: Powerful models come through a console and an API, with no hardware to buy and no research team needed. Developers start with a few API calls, and non-technical staff can use Amazon Quick.

front: Why do Bedrock features like Knowledge Bases and Guardrails improve speed to market?
back: They are ready-made building blocks for RAG and safety filters, so a team can build a prototype in days instead of months.

front: How are AWS GenAI services cost-effective compared with buying hardware?
back: You pay for what you use, for example per token, instead of paying up front for expensive hardware, and you can stop at any time.

front: What does AWS say happens to your prompts and outputs on Amazon Bedrock?
back: They are not shared with model providers and are not used to improve the base models. A model you tune is a private copy for you. Distrust answer choices that claim the opposite.

front: Name ways Amazon Bedrock supports security.
back: Data is encrypted in transit and at rest, with customer-managed keys through AWS KMS. Private connectivity from your VPC uses AWS PrivateLink. IAM controls access and CloudTrail logs activity.

front: Under shared responsibility, who secures what for a fully managed GenAI service?
back: AWS secures the infrastructure that runs the service. You control your own content: IAM permissions, encryption settings, logging, what goes into prompts and what your application does with the output.

front: Is 'AWS handles all security' a correct answer for a managed service like Bedrock?
back: No. Even with a managed service, you still own access control, data choices, Region choices and configuration to meet your own regulations.

front: Which Bedrock tools support responsible use and safety?
back: Guardrails add safeguards that help block harmful content. Evaluations compare models on quality and safety. Responsible AI is covered in depth in Domain 4.

front: A customized model on Amazon Bedrock needs which pricing option, and how is it billed?
back: Provisioned Throughput: reserved capacity at a fixed hourly price per model unit. You pay whether or not it is used, and billing continues until you delete it.

front: On-demand versus Provisioned Throughput: when does each fit?
back: On-demand is pay-per-token with no commitment, best for low or unpredictable traffic. Provisioned Throughput suits steady, high traffic that needs predictable performance. Longer commitments of 1 or 6 months lower the hourly price.

front: What is the cost of choosing a bigger model?
back: Higher capability, but more cost per token and slower answers. If a smaller model meets the requirement, it is usually the right choice.

front: Cairnway's EU chats must stay in Europe. Which cross-Region inference profile fits?
back: A geographic profile, which keeps processing within a geography such as the EU. A global profile can be cheaper, with approximately 10% savings, but may route to any supported Region.

front: What does cross-Region inference do, and does it cost extra to route?
back: Bedrock routes a request to another Region through an inference profile, to handle more traffic and improve availability. There is no additional routing cost. Inference profiles do not support Provisioned Throughput.

front: Why can regional coverage limit a GenAI design?
back: Models and features are not offered in every AWS Region, so the Regions you are allowed or want to use may not have the model you need.
